Chewy bánh bèo and a friendly chef
Oct 2026 • Solo
I was traveling independently and stopped by for a meal on my own in mid-October. I ordered the 95k portion of bánh bèo, which was soft, chewy, and fragrant. I also had a homemade lemonade, which had a nice, refreshing sourness. What I enjoyed most was chatting with the chef, who came out and shared how he learned to cook from his mother. The restaurant was a little crowded and noisy during peak hours, but overall, I had a very nice experience.

A Pretty Good Lunch With My Best Friend
Oct 2026 • Friends
My best friend was craving Central Vietnamese food, so we decided to come to Den Long for lunch. The restaurant is really cute, with plenty of nice little corners for photos, so we had fun taking a few pictures while waiting. We ordered shrimp cooked in coconut sauce with steamed rice. The dish arrived hot and smelled amazing, with a creamy coconut flavor that went really well with the rice. We waited around 20 minutes for the food, which felt a little long at first. Luckily, the staff kept refilling our iced tea and checking on us, so it made the wait easier. We’ll probably come back with the rest of our friends next time.

A Good Place for a Business Meeting
Sep 2026 • Business
I chose Den Long for a meeting with a business partner because I wanted somewhere that felt professional but still warm and comfortable. The interior is tastefully decorated, the lighting is pleasant, and the tables have enough space between them to have a private conversation. The crab curry was probably my favorite dish. It had a rich coconut flavor without any strong fishy taste. My business partner, who is from overseas, also complimented the attentive service. The only inconvenience was parking, as we had to walk a short distance to reach the restaurant. Other than that, it was a good setting for a business dinner.

A Nice Lunch After Walking Around the Old Quarter
Sep 2026 • Solo
I was walking around the Old Quarter, looking at all the Mid-Autumn Festival decorations and toys, and eventually got pretty hungry, so I stopped here for lunch. The inside was much more peaceful than I expected, and it felt relaxing as soon as I walked in. The staff were thoughtful enough to ask about allergies and preferences before recommending dishes, which I appreciated. I ordered coconut rice with shrimp sauce. The rice was fragrant and slightly sticky, while the shrimp had a creamy, rich flavor that went really well with it. It was a little expensive for a student budget, but for an occasional meal, I thought it was worth trying.

An Old Favorite That Still Feels the Same
Sep 2026 • Friends
About three years ago, our group used to come here almost every week, so when we had a chance to return to Hanoi, we had to come back. What I really liked was that the flavors still felt almost the same as I remembered. We ordered quite a few dishes, from curry to shrimp cooked with coconut, and somehow managed to finish everything. The iced tea was refreshing too, especially with the warm weather at the end of September. The staff were still friendly and helpful, and they gave us some good suggestions when choosing dishes. It was nice to revisit an old favorite and find that it still holds up.

A Relaxing Vietnamese Lunch With the Family
Sep 2026 • Family
We brought the kids to Hanoi for the Mid-Autumn Festival and decided to stop at Den Long for lunch. The restaurant has a slightly vintage-style decoration and a calm atmosphere, so it was comfortable for the whole family. The dishes were nicely seasoned without being too heavy. My favorite was the caramelized stir-fried pork — the meat was tender, fragrant and not dry at all. The kids enjoyed it too and even asked for more rice. The staff were quick and attentive, and they noticed we had children and brought smaller bowls and spoons without us asking. We’d come back if we’re in Hanoi again.

A Pleasant Dinner at Den Long
Sep 2026 • Business
I visited Den Long during a business trip and was quite impressed with the service. The staff spoke English really well and were friendly and helpful, especially when assisting international guests. After dinner, one of the staff members, Han, even wrote down a list of places to check out for the Mid-Autumn Festival around the Old Quarter. Such a thoughtful little touch. The restaurant is decorated with lots of lanterns, giving it a cozy atmosphere that reminded me of a smaller version of Hoi An. The food was generally good, and I particularly enjoyed the shrimp dishes and stir-fried pork. Prices are a little higher than some nearby places, but the service definitely added value.
